```{r}
sum_dates <- function(x){
 
  cbind.data.frame(
	min= as.Date(min(unclass(as.Date(x)), na.rm=T), origin = "1970-01-01"),
	p001= as.Date(quantile(unclass(as.Date(x)), .001, na.rm=T), origin = "1970-01-01"),
	p005= as.Date(quantile(unclass(as.Date(x)), .005, na.rm=T), origin = "1970-01-01"),
	p025= as.Date(quantile(unclass(as.Date(x)), .025, na.rm=T), origin = "1970-01-01"),
	p25= as.Date(quantile(unclass(as.Date(x)), .25, na.rm=T), origin = "1970-01-01"),
	p50= as.Date(quantile(unclass(as.Date(x)), .5, na.rm=T), origin = "1970-01-01"),
	p75= as.Date(quantile(unclass(as.Date(x)), .75, na.rm=T), origin = "1970-01-01"),
	p975= as.Date(quantile(unclass(as.Date(x)), .975, na.rm=T), origin = "1970-01-01"),
	p995= as.Date(quantile(unclass(as.Date(x)), .995, na.rm=T), origin = "1970-01-01"),
	p999= as.Date(quantile(unclass(as.Date(x)), .999, na.rm=T), origin = "1970-01-01"),
	max= as.Date(max(unclass(as.Date(x)), na.rm=T), origin = "1970-01-01")
  )
}
smd_bin <- function(x,y){
  z <- x*(1-x)
  t <- y*(1-y)
  k <- sum(z,t)
  l <- k/2
  
  return((x-y)/sqrt(l))
  
}

theme_custom_sjplot2 <- function(base_size = 12, base_family = "") {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size, base_family = base_family) +
    theme(
      # Text elements
      text = element_text(size = base_size, family = base_family),
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, size = base_size * 1.2),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 10)),
      axis.title = element_text(size = base_size, face = "bold"),
      axis.text = element_text(size = base_size * 0.8),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5),
      axis.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5),
      axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 10)),
      axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 10)),
      
      # Plot layout
      plot.margin = margin(t = 20, r = 20, b = 20, l = 20),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey80"),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      legend.position = "right",
      legend.text = element_text(size = base_size * 0.8),
      legend.title = element_text(size = base_size, face = "bold"),
      legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      legend.box.background = element_rect(colour = "grey80", linetype = "solid"),
      legend.key = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = "white")
    )
}

#CountSynth functions
get_covbal_csnth<- function(countsynth){
  res <- countsynth            # pick any run
  
  dp       <- res$dataprep.main    # Synth-style 'dataprep' object
  W        <- res$unit.weight.full.sample  # CSCM weights (full sample)
  W.scm    <- res$unit.weight.SCM          # Classic SCM weights
  cf.ts    <- res$Estimates                # time-series of fits
  
return(list(
  dataprep = dp,
  W = W,
  W.scm = W.scm,
  cf.ts = cf.ts,
  ATT = res$ATT,
  ATT.scm = res$ATT.scm,
  unit.weight.SCM = res$unit.weight.SCM,
  unit.weight.full.sample = res$unit.weight.full.sample,
  covtab = data.frame(
    variable = rownames(dp$X1),
    treated = as.numeric(dp$X1),
    synthetic = as.numeric(dp$X0 %*% W),
    abs.diff = abs(dp$X1 - dp$X0 %*% W)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
    ratio = sprintf("%1.2f", treated / synthetic),
    gap_pct_ctrl = sprintf("%1.2f", abs(100 * (treated - synthetic) / synthetic)),
    treated= sprintf("%1.2f", treated),
    synthetic= sprintf("%1.2f", synthetic),
  )
))
}

prepost_rmspe_cntsh<- function(covbal_csnth,t_int){
  # Extract the results from the countSynth object
  cf.ts    <- covbal_csnth$cf.ts
  t_int    <- t_int
  
  # Calculate pre- and post-treatment RMSPE
  max_time <- max(cf.ts$time)
  
  # Create logical vectors for pre- and post-treatment periods
  pre    <- cf.ts$time <  t_int
  post   <- cf.ts$time >= t_int

  rmspe <- function(a,b) sqrt(mean((a-b)^2))
  
  pre.rmspe  <- rmspe(cf.ts$observed[pre], cf.ts$est.counterfactual[pre])
  post.rmspe <- rmspe(cf.ts$observed[post], cf.ts$est.counterfactual[post])
  ratio      <- post.rmspe / pre.rmspe
  return(
    list(
      pre_post_ratio= c(pre=pre.rmspe, post=post.rmspe, ratio=ratio)
      )
  )
}
plot_synth_cscm <- function(res_object, 
                            max_time = NULL, 
                            t_int_man,
                            y_lab = "High-speed rate",
                            colors = c("SCM" = "black", "CSCM" = "red", "Obs" = "gray60")) {
  
  # Validate inputs
  if (!inherits(res_object, "list")) stop("res_object must be a list")
  if (!all(c("dataprep.main", "unit.weight.SCM", "unit.weight.full.sample") %in% names(res_object))) {
    stop("res_object missing required components")
  }
  if (is.null(max_time)) max_time <- nrow(res_object$dataprep.main$Y0plot)
  
  # Calculate counterfactuals
  synth.orig <- res_object$dataprep.main$Y0plot %*% as.numeric(res_object$unit.weight.SCM)
  cscm.cf <- res_object$dataprep.main$Y0plot %*% as.numeric(res_object$unit.weight.full.sample)
  year <- 1:max_time
  
  # Create data frames
  adf <- data.frame(Year = year, Y = synth.orig[1:max_time], Method = "SCM")
  bdf <- data.frame(Year = year, Y = cscm.cf[1:max_time], Method = "CSCM")
  cdf <- data.frame(Year = year, Y = res_object$dataprep.main$Y1plot[1:max_time], Method = "Obs")
  
  # Combine data
  cfdf <- rbind(adf, bdf, cdf)
  
  # Create plot
  ggplot(cfdf, aes(y = Y, x = Year, group = Method, linetype = Method, color = Method)) + 
    geom_vline(xintercept = t_int_man, linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
    scale_color_manual(values = colors) +
    theme_bw() +
    labs(y = y_lab, x = "") +
    theme(
      text = element_text(size = 15),
      panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      axis.line = element_line(colour = "black"),
      legend.position = "bottom"
    # Ensure linetype scale if needed (uncomment if necessary)
    # scale_linetype_manual(values = c("SCM" = "solid", "CSCM" = "solid", "Observed" = "solid"))
    )
}
```

```{r}
#-- Fórmula 1 – ventana de riesgo
#-- Accidentes por exceso de velocidad
#--Weather (temperatura, lluvia…)
#-- Day-of-week / season / calendario
#-- Rasgos fijos de la comuna (infraestructura, cultura vial)
dag <- dagitty('
dag {
  F1   [exposure,   pos="-2.000,  0.000"]
  Y    [outcome,    pos=" 2.000,  0.000"]
  W    [adjusted,   pos="-1.000,  3.250"]
  DOW  [adjusted,   pos="-1.000, -3.250"]
  U    [unobserved, pos=" -3.000,  2.000"]

  F1  -> Y
  W   -> F1
  W   -> Y
  DOW -> F1
  DOW -> Y
  U   -> Y
}
')
# coords <- data.frame(
#   x = c(-2,  2, -1, -1,  3),   # ← exactly the positions you want
#   y = c( 0,  0,  3, -3,  0),
#   row.names = c("F1", "Y", "W", "DOW", "U")
# )
# 
# coordinates(dag) <- coords     # fix positions inside dagitty

# data
tidy  <- tidy_dagitty(dag)

edges <- tidy %>%                      # sólo flechas →
  filter(direction == "->") %>%
  mutate(
    edge_colour    = if_else(name == "U", "grey60", "black"),
    edge_linetype  = if_else(name == "U", "dashed",  "solid"),
    edge_linewidth = 0.9                               # grosor
  )

nodes <- tidy %>% data.frame() |>  distinct(name, x, y) %>%             # nodos
  mutate(shape = if_else(name %in% c("W","DOW"),
                         "square", "circle"))

## 3 · Plot -------------------------------------------------------------
ggplot() +
  geom_dag_edges_link(                     # ← solo flechas →
    data = edges,
    aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend,
        edge_colour    = edge_colour,
        edge_linetype  = edge_linetype,
        edge_linewidth = edge_linewidth)
  ) +
  geom_dag_node(
    data = nodes,
    aes(x = x, y = y, shape = shape),
    fill   = "white", colour = "black", size = 18
  ) +
  geom_dag_text(data = nodes, aes(x = x, y = y, label = name)) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(square = 15, circle = 16)) + 
  #scale_edge_colour_identity() +
  #scale_edge_linetype_identity() +
  #edge_width_identity() +   # usa edge_width_identity() si tu ggraph ≤ 2.0
  theme_void()+
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

```{r}
cities <- unique(collisions_weather_corr$cluster)
for (c in cities) {
  cat("\nEvaluando autocorrelación para cluster:", c, "\n")
  
  city_data <- collisions_weather_corr %>% filter(cluster == c) %>% arrange(iso_yday)
  
  indices <- which(collisions_weather_corr$cluster == c)
  city_residuals <- simulationOutput$scaledResiduals[indices]
  
  # Verificar que city_data y city_residuals tengan la misma longitud
  if(length(city_residuals) != nrow(city_data)) {
    cat("Error: longitud de residuos y datos no coincide para cluster:", c, "\n")
    next
  }
  
  # Verificar que no haya NA en residuos ni en fechas
  if(any(is.na(city_residuals)) || any(is.na(city_data$date))) {
    cat("Error: NA en residuos o fechas para cluster:", c, "\n")
    next
  }
  
  # Ordenar residuos según fechas
  order_idx <- order(city_data$iso_yday)
  city_data <- city_data[order_idx, ]
  city_residuals <- city_residuals[order_idx]
  
  print(paste("Length residuos:", length(city_residuals)))
  print(paste("Length fechas:", length(city_data$date)))
  print(paste("Duplicados fechas:", any(duplicated(city_data$date))))
  print(paste("NA en residuos:", sum(is.na(city_residuals))))
  
  # Verificar que fechas estén ordenadas y sin duplicados
  if(any(duplicated(city_data$date))) {
    cat("Error: fechas duplicadas para cluster:", c, "\n")
    next
  }
  
  # Finalmente, llamar a la función
  tryCatch({
    testTemporalAutocorrelation(city_residuals, time = city_data$date)
    mtext(text = paste("Autocorr, cluster:", c), side = 3, line = 3, cex = 1.2, font = 2)
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("Error en testTemporalAutocorrelation para cluster:", c, "\n", e$message, "\n")
  })
}

invisible("No hay evidencia significativa de autocorrelación temporal en los residuos del modelo para ninguna de las ciudades.")
```

```{r}
geeM_pois_m2 <- geem(

    max_temp_mean_lin + total_precip_median_lin,

  corstr  = "m-dependent",
  M       = 40,                 # correlaciones solo hasta lag 2
  family  = poisson(link = "log"),
  data    = collisions_weather_corr,
  scale.fix = FALSE
)
summary(geeM_pois_m2)
```

```{r}
# Crear dataset contrafactual (exposure = 0 para todos los días)
data_cf <- data %>% mutate(exposure = 0)

# Predicciones observadas
pred_obs <- posterior_predict(bayes_model, newdata = data, summary = TRUE)

# Predicciones contrafactuales
pred_cf <- posterior_predict(bayes_model, newdata = data_cf, summary = TRUE)

# Agregar resultados al dataset original
data$pred_obs_mean <- pred_obs[, "Estimate"]
data$pred_cf_mean <- pred_cf[, "Estimate"]

ggplot(data, aes(x = date)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = pred_obs_mean, color = "Observado")) +
  geom_line(aes(y = pred_cf_mean, color = "Contrafactual (sin exposición)")) +
  facet_wrap(~ city, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(y = "Número esperado de tickets", x = "Fecha",
       title = "Evolución observada vs contrafactual por ciudad",
       color = "Escenario") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
# Methods:
# Only cases: cardiovascular defects 3870

# Exposure:
# Case window: trimethoprim use any time during the second
# 	and third months after the last menstrual period,
# Reference window: use in 2 months prior to last menstrual
# 	period within mothers of case infants.
# Secondary reference windows: and 2 months prior and 2
# 	months after the primary reference window
```

```{r}
#| class-output: center-table
#| message: true
#| include: true
#| warning: true
#| error: true
#| label: test-association-gnm
#| eval: true
#| results: "hold"
#Factor variable that identifies each case-control block
#Ej.: interaction(ciudad, mes, día_semana) o id_persona en estudios de eventos agudos.

## ── Helper para φ  (sobre‑dispersión) ──────────────────────────────────────────
get_phi <- function(mod) {
  max( sum(residuals(mod, type = "pearson")^2) / df.residual(mod), 1 )  # ≤1 ⇒ 1
}

## ── Función QIC para modelos gnm quasi‑Poisson ────────────────────────────────
qic_gnm <- function(mod_quasi) {
  ## 1)  φ desde el quasi
  phi <- get_phi(mod_quasi)

  ## 2)  refit Poisson (mismo call)  → logLik disponible
  mod_pois <- update(mod_quasi, family = poisson)

  ## 3)  qAIC = -2·logLik/φ + 2·k    (bbmle lo hace por ti)
  bbmle::qAIC(mod_pois, dispersion = phi)
}

  "Treated + lead 1"          = qic_gnm_tratados_lead1,
  "Treated + lead 2"          = qic_gnm_tratados_lead2,
  "Treated sensitivity (- Sherbrooke)"      = qic_gnm_tratados_sens,
  "Treated sens + lead 1"     = qic_gnm_tratados_lead1_sens,
  "Treated sens + lead 2"     = qic_gnm_tratados_lead2_sens,
  "Controls (base)"           = qic_gnm_controles,
  "Controls + lead 1"         = qic_gnm_controles_lead1,
  "Controls + lead 2"         = qic_gnm_controles_lead2,
  "Controls sensitivity (+ Sherbrooke)"     = qic_gnm_controles_sens,
  "Controls sens + lead 1"    = qic_gnm_controles_lead1_sens,
  "Controls sens + lead 2"    = qic_gnm_controles_lead2_sens
)

## ─── 3. print results ───────────────────────────────────────
cat(
  "\n≡ Comparison of models through QIC (quasi‑AIC) ≡",
  "\n(‑2·ℓ / φ  +  2·k ;  lower ⇒ better)\n\n",
  paste(names(qic_vec), sprintf(": %.1f", qic_vec), collapse = "\n"),
  "\n\n≡ Ranking (better → worse) ≡\n",
  paste(names(sort(qic_vec)), sprintf(": %.1f", sort(qic_vec)), collapse = "\n"),
  "\n"
)
```

```{r}
cat("Added the Lag Y by status and year:\n")
collisions_weather_corr_rect_synth_one_tr_many_cntrls$Y_lag10 <- 
collisions_weather_corr_rect_synth_one_tr_many_cntrls|> 
    group_by(tr_contr_sens, year.x)|> 
    mutate(Y_lag10 = dplyr::lag(rate_veh, 10, order_by = yday_corr))|> 
    ungroup()|>
    pull(Y_lag10) 
collisions_weather_corr_rect_quebec_synth_one_tr_many_cntrls$Y_lag10 <-

    group_by(tr_contr, year.x)|> 
    mutate(Y_lag10 = dplyr::lag(rate_veh, 4, order_by = yday_corr))|> 
    ungroup()|>
    pull(Y_lag10)

collisions_weather_corr_rect_synth_one_tr_many_cntrls|>
  mutate(intersect= paste0(id,"_",year.x)) |> 
    group_by(intersect)|>
    mutate(
        third_value = nth(na.omit(Y_lag10), 1),
        Y_lag10 = ifelse(is.na(Y_lag10), third_value, Y_lag10)
    )|>
```

- The pre-treatment balance diagnostics show an excellent fit between treated and its synthetic control.  The absolute gaps in the main predictors translate into relative differences of ≤ 10 %.  Crucially, the two variables that receive virtually all the weight in the V-matrix—current precipitation and precipitation lagged two days—match almost perfectly (≤ 0.3 % gap), as does the 10-day lag of the outcome. Overall, the synthetic control replicates the treated unit’s pre-grand prix trajectory very closely, so the absence of a post-event divergence cannot be attributed to poor pre-treatment balance.*
- Units 6, 7, 14, 20 explain more than 97% of the synthetic control (w.weights). For Quebec only as controls, donor units 7, 15, 6, 20, 2 explain 79% of the synthetic control.
- The effect post Grand Prix does not differentiate compared to the pseudo-treated units. There is no evidence of an unusual causal effect.
- Ratios of RMSPE (root mean squared prediction errors) post/pre-intervention and the proportion of control units with ratios greater or equal to treated does not detect a causal effect.

### CountSynth

We used a new **synthetic-control tool for counts and other non-negative numbers**. It matches the pre-treatment path like usual, but its error rule lets it stretch—while penalizing—any needed extrapolation. No log tricks or “+1” fixes are needed, so predictions stay non-negative even when the data include zeros  [@Bonander2021] [https://youtu.be/e5hmK5GzCHc](https://youtu.be/e5hmK5GzCHc).


#### Instantaneous effect

```{r}

source(paste0(getwd(),"/_funcs/CSCM_helper_functions.R"))
#Bonander, Carl. A (Flexible) Synthetic Control Method for Count Data and Other Nonnegative Outcomes. Epidemiology 32(5):p 653-660, September 2021. | DOI: 10.1097/EDE.0000000000001388

packages <- c("ggplot2", "Synth", "glmnet",
              "dplyr", "osqp", "optimx")
if (length(setdiff(packages, rownames(installed.packages()))) > 0) {

}
```

```{r}
#| class-output: center-table
#| message: true
#| include: true
#| warning: true
#| error: true
#| label: synth3
#| eval: true
#| results: hold
#| fig.width: 12
#K= Number of non-overlapping hold-out blocks (“folds”) used for cross-fitting the weights and penalty. More folds ⇒ less bias but higher variance and longer run time.
#When countSynth tunes its ridge/elastic-net penalty (λ) by cross-validation, this flag tells it not to use the “one–standard-error” rule. If you set it to TRUE, the algorithm would pick the most parsimonious λ within 1 s.e. of the CV minimum.

#prepost_rmspe_cntsh(get_covbal_csnth(road.main.res), t_int=38)

result_objects <- list(
  list(obj = road.main.res, name = "road.main.res", desc = "0,+7 ; Quebec+Sherbrook as control"),
  list(obj = road.main.res_35, name = "road.main.res_35", desc = "-2,+7 ; Quebec+Sherbrook as control"),
  list(obj = road.main.res_q, name = "road.main.res_q", desc = "0,+7 ; Quebec only as control"),
  list(obj = road.main.res_35, name = "road.main.res_35_repeat", desc = "-2,+7 ; Quebec+Sherbrook as control (Repeat)"),
  list(obj = road.main.res_35_38, name = "road.main.res_35_38", desc = "-2,+3 ; Quebec+Sherbrook as control"),
  list(obj = road.main.res_q_38, name = "road.main.res_q_38", desc = "0,+3 ; Quebec only as control"),
  list(obj = road.main.res_q_35_38, name = "road.main.res_q_35_38", desc = "-2,+3 ; Quebec only as control"),

  # Penalized Models
  list(obj = road.main.res1se, name = "road.main.res1se", desc = "Penalized, 0,+7 ; Quebec+Sherbrook as control"),
  list(obj = road.main.res_351se, name = "road.main.res_351se", desc = "Penalized, -2,+7 ; Quebec+Sherbrook as control"),
  list(obj = road.main.res_q1se, name = "road.main.res_q1se", desc = "Penalized, 0,+7 ; Quebec only as control"),
  list(obj = road.main.res_351se, name = "road.main.res_351se_repeat", desc = "Penalized, -2,+7 ; Quebec+Sherbrook as control (Repeat)"),
  list(obj = road.main.res_35_381se, name = "road.main.res_35_381se", desc = "Penalized, -2,+3 ; Quebec+Sherbrook as control"),
  list(obj = road.main.res_q_381se, name = "road.main.res_q_381se", desc = "Penalized, 0,+3 ; Quebec only as control"),
  list(obj = road.main.res_q_35_381se, name = "road.main.res_q_35_381se", desc = "Penalized, -2,+3 ; Quebec only as control")
)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Loop through objects, print ATT, and create/store plots
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Initialize an empty list to store the generated ggplot objects.
plot_list <- list()

# This loop iterates over each item in the `result_objects` list.
for (item in result_objects) {

  # --- Print the ATT Value ---
  cat("--------------------------------------------------\n")
  cat("Processing:", item$name, "\n")
  cat(item$desc, "\n")
  print(item$obj$ATT)
  cat("\n")

  # --- Generate and Store the Plot ---
  # Check if the object exists to prevent errors
  if (exists(item$name) && !is.null(get(item$name))) {

    # Call the plotting function which returns a ggplot object
    p <- plot_synth_cscm(
      res_object = item$obj,
      t_int_man = 38,       # Manual intervention time
      max_time = 45,        # Time horizon for the plot
      y_lab = "Crash rate", # Y-axis label
      colors = c("SCM" = "gray60", "CSCM" = "red", "Obs" = "black")
    )

    # Add the title using ggplot2's labs() function and store it
    plot_list[[item$name]] <- p + labs(title = item$desc) + theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 13))

  } else {
    cat("Warning: Object", item$name, "not found. Skipping plot generation.\n")
  }
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Arrange and display the plots in 2x2 grids using cowplot
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Now, print the combined plots. In a Quarto/Rmd file, this will render
# the grids directly in the output document.
print(plot_grid(plotlist = plot_list[1:4], ncol = 2, nrow = 2))

print(plot_grid(plotlist = plot_list[5:8], ncol = 2, nrow = 2))

print(plot_grid(plotlist = plot_list[9:12], ncol = 2, nrow = 2))
```

```{r}
#| class-output: center-table
#| message: true
#| include: true
#| warning: true
#| error: true
#| label: synth3_lead1
#| eval: true
#| results: hold
#| fig.width: 12
#K= Number of non-overlapping hold-out blocks (“folds”) used for cross-fitting the weights and penalty. More folds ⇒ less bias but higher variance and longer run time.
#When countSynth tunes its ridge/elastic-net penalty (λ) by cross-validation, this flag tells it not to use the “one–standard-error” rule. If you set it to TRUE, the algorithm would pick the most parsimonious λ within 1 s.e. of the CV minimum.

#prepost_rmspe_cntsh(get_covbal_csnth(road.main.res), t_int=38)

result_objects2 <- list(
  list(obj = road.main.res_lead1, name = "road.main.res", desc = "0,+7 ; Quebec+Sherbrook as control"),
  list(obj = road.main.res_35_lead1, name = "road.main.res_35", desc = "-2,+7 ; Quebec+Sherbrook as control"),
  list(obj = road.main.res_q_lead1, name = "road.main.res_q", desc = "0,+7 ; Quebec only as control"),
  list(obj = road.main.res_35_lead1, name = "road.main.res_35_repeat", desc = "-2,+7 ; Quebec+Sherbrook as control (Repeat)"),
  list(obj = road.main.res_35_38_lead1, name = "road.main.res_35_38", desc = "-2,+3 ; Quebec+Sherbrook as control"),
  list(obj = road.main.res_q_38_lead1, name = "road.main.res_q_38", desc = "0,+3 ; Quebec only as control"),
  list(obj = road.main.res_q_35_38_lead1, name = "road.main.res_q_35_38", desc = "-2,+3 ; Quebec only as control"),

  # Penalized Models
  list(obj = road.main.res1se_lead1, name = "road.main.res1se", desc = "Penalized, 0,+7 ; Quebec+Sherbrook as control"),
  list(obj = road.main.res_351se_lead1, name = "road.main.res_351se", desc = "Penalized, -2,+7 ; Quebec+Sherbrook as control"),
  list(obj = road.main.res_q1se_lead1, name = "road.main.res_q1se", desc = "Penalized, 0,+7 ; Quebec only as control"),
  list(obj = road.main.res_351se_lead1, name = "road.main.res_351se_repeat", desc = "Penalized, -2,+7 ; Quebec+Sherbrook as control (Repeat)"),
  list(obj = road.main.res_35_381se_lead1, name = "road.main.res_35_381se", desc = "Penalized, -2,+3 ; Quebec+Sherbrook as control"),
  list(obj = road.main.res_q_381se_lead1, name = "road.main.res_q_381se", desc = "Penalized, 0,+3 ; Quebec only as control"),
  list(obj = road.main.res_q_35_381se_lead1, name = "road.main.res_q_35_381se", desc = "Penalized, -2,+3 ; Quebec only as control")
)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Loop through objects, print ATT, and create/store plots
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Initialize an empty list to store the generated ggplot objects.
plot_list2 <- list()

# This loop iterates over each item in the `result_objects` list.
for (item in result_objects2) {

  # --- Print the ATT Value ---
  cat("--------------------------------------------------\n")
  cat("Processing:", item$name, "\n")
  cat(item$desc, "\n")
  print(item$obj$ATT)
  cat("\n")

  # --- Generate and Store the Plot ---
  # Check if the object exists to prevent errors
  if (exists(item$name) && !is.null(get(item$name))) {

    # Call the plotting function which returns a ggplot object
    p <- plot_synth_cscm(
      res_object = item$obj,
      t_int_man = 38,       # Manual intervention time
      max_time = 45,        # Time horizon for the plot
      y_lab = "Crash rate", # Y-axis label
      colors = c("SCM" = "gray60", "CSCM" = "red", "Obs" = "black")
    )

    # Add the title using ggplot2's labs() function and store it
    plot_list2[[item$name]] <- p + labs(title = item$desc) + theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 13))

  } else {
    cat("Warning: Object", item$name, "not found. Skipping plot generation.\n")
  }
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Arrange and display the plots in 2x2 grids using cowplot
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Now, print the combined plots. In a Quarto/Rmd file, this will render
# the grids directly in the output document.
print(plot_grid(plotlist = plot_list2[1:4], ncol = 2, nrow = 2))

print(plot_grid(plotlist = plot_list2[5:8], ncol = 2, nrow = 2))

print(plot_grid(plotlist = plot_list2[9:12], ncol = 2, nrow = 2))
```

```{r}
#| class-output: center-table
#| message: true
#| include: true
#| warning: true
#| error: true
#| label: synth3_lead2
#| eval: true
#| results: hold
#| fig.width: 12
#K= Number of non-overlapping hold-out blocks (“folds”) used for cross-fitting the weights and penalty. More folds ⇒ less bias but higher variance and longer run time.
#When countSynth tunes its ridge/elastic-net penalty (λ) by cross-validation, this flag tells it not to use the “one–standard-error” rule. If you set it to TRUE, the algorithm would pick the most parsimonious λ within 1 s.e. of the CV minimum.

#prepost_rmspe_cntsh(get_covbal_csnth(road.main.res), t_int=38)

result_objects3 <- list(
  list(obj = road.main.res_lead2, name = "road.main.res", desc = "0,+7 ; Quebec+Sherbrook as control"),
  list(obj = road.main.res_35_lead2, name = "road.main.res_35", desc = "-2,+7 ; Quebec+Sherbrook as control"),
  list(obj = road.main.res_q_lead2, name = "road.main.res_q", desc = "0,+7 ; Quebec only as control"),
  list(obj = road.main.res_35_lead2, name = "road.main.res_35_repeat", desc = "-2,+7 ; Quebec+Sherbrook as control (Repeat)"),
  list(obj = road.main.res_35_38_lead2, name = "road.main.res_35_38", desc = "-2,+3 ; Quebec+Sherbrook as control"),
  list(obj = road.main.res_q_38_lead2, name = "road.main.res_q_38", desc = "0,+3 ; Quebec only as control"),
  list(obj = road.main.res_q_35_38_lead2, name = "road.main.res_q_35_38", desc = "-2,+3 ; Quebec only as control"),

  # Penalized Models
  list(obj = road.main.res1se_lead2, name = "road.main.res1se", desc = "Penalized, 0,+7 ; Quebec+Sherbrook as control"),
  list(obj = road.main.res_351se_lead2, name = "road.main.res_351se", desc = "Penalized, -2,+7 ; Quebec+Sherbrook as control"),
  list(obj = road.main.res_q1se_lead2, name = "road.main.res_q1se", desc = "Penalized, 0,+7 ; Quebec only as control"),
  list(obj = road.main.res_351se_lead2, name = "road.main.res_351se_repeat", desc = "Penalized, -2,+7 ; Quebec+Sherbrook as control (Repeat)"),
  list(obj = road.main.res_35_381se_lead2, name = "road.main.res_35_381se", desc = "Penalized, -2,+3 ; Quebec+Sherbrook as control"),
  list(obj = road.main.res_q_381se_lead2, name = "road.main.res_q_381se", desc = "Penalized, 0,+3 ; Quebec only as control"),
  list(obj = road.main.res_q_35_381se_lead2, name = "road.main.res_q_35_381se", desc = "Penalized, -2,+3 ; Quebec only as control")
)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Loop through objects, print ATT, and create/store plots
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Initialize an empty list to store the generated ggplot objects.
plot_list3 <- list()

# This loop iterates over each item in the `result_objects` list.
for (item in result_objects3) {

  # --- Print the ATT Value ---
  cat("--------------------------------------------------\n")
  cat("Processing:", item$name, "\n")
  cat(item$desc, "\n")
  print(item$obj$ATT)
  cat("\n")

  # --- Generate and Store the Plot ---
  # Check if the object exists to prevent errors
  if (exists(item$name) && !is.null(get(item$name))) {

    # Call the plotting function which returns a ggplot object
    p <- plot_synth_cscm(
      res_object = item$obj,
      t_int_man = 38,       # Manual intervention time
      max_time = 45,        # Time horizon for the plot
      y_lab = "Crash rate", # Y-axis label
      colors = c("SCM" = "gray60", "CSCM" = "red", "Obs" = "black")
    )

    # Add the title using ggplot2's labs() function and store it
    plot_list3[[item$name]] <- p + labs(title = item$desc) + theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 13))

  } else {
    cat("Warning: Object", item$name, "not found. Skipping plot generation.\n")
  }
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Arrange and display the plots in 2x2 grids using cowplot
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Now, print the combined plots. In a Quarto/Rmd file, this will render
# the grids directly in the output document.
print(plot_grid(plotlist = plot_list3[1:4], ncol = 2, nrow = 2))

print(plot_grid(plotlist = plot_list3[5:8], ncol = 2, nrow = 2))

print(plot_grid(plotlist = plot_list3[9:12], ncol = 2, nrow = 2))
```
